summary: Extracts badge-table rendering into shared helpers in github_render.py so the sticky's 'This run' section and the per-review body draw the same primary row from one source and cannot drift.

pr_summary.headline: Extracts badge-table rendering into shared helpers in github_render.py so the sticky's 'This run' section and the per-review body draw the same primary row from one source and cannot drift.

walkthrough.text: Three new public functions and a private helper land in github_render.py: _escape_cell (pipe/backslash/line-break sanitization), format_badge_table (single-row table), format_badge_tables (stacked tables with blank-line separation), and run_stats_primary_cells (the shared model/cost/token cell list).

github_review_body.py removes its private _badge_table function and rewires _run_stats_section to delegate to format_badge_tables and run_stats_primary_cells, keeping the per-review body output byte-identical for typical inputs.
github_sticky.py replaces the two prose bullet lines in _this_run_section with a '**This run**' heading and two single-row badge tables, matching the visual style of the per-review body.

A new test file (test_github_badge_tables.py) pins the helper contract, ordering rule, tilde-prefix logic, pipe/backslash escaping, line-break flattening, and a full snapshot of the sticky's This-run block; one existing assertion in test_github_sticky_mission_control.py is updated to expect table headers and value rows instead of the old prose line.
_fmt_int and _fmt_cost remain imported and used elsewhere in github_sticky.py (history section), so the sticky's import block is still clean after the change.

verdict_reasoning.deciding_factor: No P1 or P2 issues were found. The refactoring is clean: _badge_table is deleted rather than duplicated, run_stats_primary_cells is the single source of truth for the primary row, and format_badge_tables correctly inserts one blank line between stacked tables. The one P3 finding is that _escape_cell escapes | unconditionally without distinguishing GFM code-span boundaries, so a model name containing | would display with a literal backslash artifact inside the code chip. No real model name from any provider contains |, so this is a theoretical concern that does not block the merge.

New test file covering the badge-table helper contract, ordering, tilde prefixes, pipe/backslash escaping, line-break flattening, and a full snapshot of the sticky's This-run block.
Updates one assertion from the old '**This run** — model ...' prose format to the new table header and value rows.

findings.title: Pipe escape in code-span values produces backslash display artifact
findings.description: _escape_cell escapes | unconditionally. Per CommonMark (which GitHub's GFM implements), a | inside a backtick code span is already protected from being treated as a cell separator because code spans have higher parsing priority than table-cell splitting. When _escape_cell is called on a value already wrapped in backticks — as run_stats_primary_cells does for the model cell (line 162: f"`{sanitize_comment_text(metadata.model, limit=60)}`") — the escape is redundant for row-integrity purposes and harmful for display: a model name containing | (e.g. org/model|v2) becomes `org/model\|v2`, which GitHub renders inside the code chip as the literal text org/model\|v2 (backslash visible) rather than org/model|v2. The format_badge_table docstring at line 100 claims 'GFM honors \| inside code spans too,' which is correct in the narrow sense that the escape prevents row shearing, but omits that it simultaneously corrupts the displayed text inside the chip.
findings.cause: _escape_cell performs a naive string-level replacement with no awareness of code-span boundaries. format_badge_table then applies it to every cell value, including values whose callers have already wrapped in backticks. The test at test_github_badge_tables.py:87 passes `'`a|b`'` and expects `'| `a\\|b` |'` — it verifies the current (artifact-producing) behavior rather than the correct behavior, locking in the display regression.
findings.fix: Apply pipe escaping before wrapping the model name in backticks, not after. In run_stats_primary_cells, compute the escaped model string first and then wrap: escaped_model = metadata.model.replace('|', '\\|'); return [('model', f'`{sanitize_comment_text(escaped_model, limit=60)}`'), ...]. Alternatively, rely on GFM's code-span protection and remove the .replace('|', '\\|') step from _escape_cell for code-chipped callers by providing a separate escape variant that handles only non-code-span content. At minimum, correct the docstring so it does not claim the current behavior is display-correct.
